q: GDP is the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period.
Inflation in India is most commonly measured using the:
The CPI measures retail price changes and is the RBI's main inflation target measure.
Fiscal deficit is the gap between:
Government expenditure and total receipts excluding borrowings
Fiscal deficit shows how much the government needs to borrow to meet its spending.
A sustained fall in the general price level is called:
Deflation is a persistent fall in prices. Disinflation is a slowdown in the rate of inflation.
Microeconomics focuses on individual decision-makers, prices in specific markets and resource allocation.
According to the law of demand, other things being equal, when price rises:
Price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions, giving a downward-sloping demand curve.
Real GDP differs from nominal GDP because real GDP is adjusted for:
Real GDP uses constant prices to remove the effect of price changes, making growth comparisons meaningful.
Per capita income is calculated as:
Per capita income is a rough measure of average income per person.
A situation of high inflation with stagnant growth is called:
Stagflation combines slow growth and high unemployment with rising prices.
Which is a primary sector activity?
The primary sector extracts natural resources through farming, mining, fishing and forestry.
Primary deficit shows borrowing needs excluding past interest obligations.
A recession is generally defined as:
Two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth
Two successive quarters of contracting GDP is a common technical definition of recession.
Which organisation publishes India's National Accounts Statistics?
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
MoSPI compiles national accounts, including GDP estimates.
The base year currently used for India's GDP series is:
India's national accounts use 2011-12 as the base year for the current series.
Which of these is a macroeconomics variable?
Price of one brand of soap
Macroeconomics studies aggregates such as national income, inflation, unemployment and trade.
The Union Budget is presented in Parliament under which Article?
Article 112 requires the President to lay the Annual Financial Statement before Parliament.
The Union Budget is normally presented on:
Since 2017, the Union Budget has been presented on 1 February, ahead of the new financial year.
Who presents the Union Budget in Parliament?
The Finance Minister presents the Union Budget, usually on 1 February.
Direct taxes are paid directly by the taxpayer, such as income tax. GST and customs are indirect taxes.
GST was implemented in India on:
GST came into effect on 1 July 2017 through the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
The Union Finance Minister chairs the GST Council, with state finance ministers as members.
The Indian financial year is April to March; the Budget is prepared for this period.
Revenue deficit measures the shortfall in revenue receipts compared with revenue expenditure.
Capital expenditure creates assets or reduces liabilities, such as roads, bridges and machinery.
A Vote on Account is used to:
Meet expenses until the Budget is passed
A Vote on Account lets the government withdraw money for a few months until the full Budget is approved.
GST is a destination-based, multi-stage indirect tax on consumption.
A cess is a tax that is:
Cess is earmarked for a specific purpose, such as education or health, and is not shared with states in the usual way.
Fiscal policy is managed mainly by:
Fiscal policy covers government taxation and spending; monetary policy is managed by the RBI.
Which tax is levied on the manufacture and sale of goods within a state before GST?
Excise duty was a central tax on manufacture, largely subsumed into GST in 2017.
Zero-based budgeting requires every expenditure to be:
Zero-based budgeting starts from a zero base rather than last year's allocation, requiring fresh justification.
The Reserve Bank of India was established in:
The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 and nationalised in 1949.
The headquarters of the RBI is in:
The RBI's central office is in Mumbai. It was initially in Kolkata.
The repo rate is the rate at which:
The RBI lends short-term funds to banks
The government borrows from the IMF
Repo is the RBI's short-term lending rate to banks against government securities.
CRR is the share of deposits banks must keep with the RBI as cash reserves.
SLR is the minimum share of deposits banks must hold in liquid assets such as government securities.
The Monetary Policy Committee of India has how many members?
The MPC has six members, including the RBI Governor as chairperson.
India's flexible inflation targeting framework sets a 4% CPI target with a tolerance band of 2-6%.
Which is India's apex development bank for agriculture?
NABARD supports agriculture and rural development. SIDBI focuses on small industries.
Nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks took place in:
Fourteen major banks were nationalised in 1969; six more were nationalised in 1980.
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) operates UPI, RuPay and other retail payment systems.
A scheduled bank is one that:
Is included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act
Scheduled banks are listed in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act and meet certain capital and operational conditions.
The RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949.
Which instrument is used by the RBI to absorb liquidity from the banking system?
In reverse repo, banks park surplus funds with the RBI, absorbing liquidity.
Access to affordable financial services for all
Only opening bank accounts for the rich
Financial inclusion aims to give everyone access to banking, credit, insurance and payments.
The RBI Governor is appointed by:
The Central Government appoints the RBI Governor, usually for a three-year term.
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana aims at:
PMJDY, launched in 2014, provides basic savings accounts, insurance and overdraft facilities.
Ayushman Bharat provides health cover of:
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY offers ₹5 lakh annual health cover for eligible families.
100 days of wage employment in rural areas
The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2005 guarantees 100 days of unskilled wage work per rural household.
PM-KISAN gives direct income support to eligible farmer families in instalments.
Ujjwala provides LPG connections to women from below-poverty-line households to promote clean cooking fuel.
Swachh Bharat Mission was launched in:
Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014 to improve sanitation and eliminate open defecation.
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana aims to provide:
PMAY supports affordable housing for urban and rural families.
APY provides a guaranteed pension to subscribers from the unorganised sector after age 60.
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is aimed at:
The scheme encourages savings for a girl child's education and marriage through a small savings account.
Startup India was launched in January 2016 to encourage entrepreneurship and simplify compliance.
Make in India was launched in:
Make in India was launched in September 2014 to boost manufacturing and investment.
Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana provides:
PMFBY insures farmers against crop loss from natural calamities, pests and diseases.
Skill India Mission was launched in:
Skill India was launched in July 2015 to provide skill training and improve employability.
Digital India, launched in 2015, promotes digital infrastructure, governance and literacy.
PM Vishwakarma, launched in 2023, provides training, loans and support to traditional artisans and craftspeople.
